_comment: Annotated example for poll_connector.py --config, targeting Elastic Security's own detection-alerts index via Elasticsearch's URI Search API -- a plain GET with a Lucene query string, which fits PollerConfig directly with no async job/create-then-poll dance needed. Point base_url at YOUR Elasticsearch endpoint and space/index name. Delete this _comment field (or leave it; it's ignored) before using.
name: elastic-security-alerts
_comment_auth: Generate an API key in Kibana (Stack Management -> API Keys) or via the Elasticsearch _security/api_key endpoint -- it comes back as an id:api_key pair; base64-encode 'id:api_key' yourself and set THAT as ELASTIC_API_KEY (auth_token_env names an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, never the key itself in this file). Elastic's own header shape is 'Authorization: ApiKey <base64>', expressed here via auth_scheme.
_comment_query: Elasticsearch's URI Search API accepts a Lucene query string via 'q', plus sort/size -- no JSON request body needed for a query this simple. Adjust the Lucene query to your own space/rule filters (e.g. add 'AND kibana.alert.rule.name:"your rule"').
_comment_records_path: Elasticsearch's _search response body is {"hits": {"hits": [{"_id": ..., "_source": {...ECS fields...}}, ...]}} -- normalize_elastic() unwraps each hit's _source itself, so records_path only needs to reach the hit list.
_comment_cursor: Elasticsearch's simple URI Search API doesn't expose a clean single cursor param the way Splunk's earliest_time or a REST API's own next-page token does -- cursor_query_param/cursor_field are deliberately left unset here. Cavendex's own CAVENDEX_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS-based dedup (keyed on each alert's real Elasticsearch document _id, via normalize_elastic()'s dedup_key) absorbs the resulting re-fetch of already-seen alerts on every poll instead.
_comment_normalizer: Uses the real Elastic Security normalizer (ingestion/normalizers.py:normalize_elastic) instead of a generic field_map -- it combines source.ip/destination.ip into one iocs list and routes real EDR-native process context (process.name/process.command_line/process.parent.name) into NormalizedAlert's dedicated process_name/command_line/parent_process_name fields, neither of which a flat field_map alone can do.
